title: Temple of Horus at Edfu
summary: The Temple of Horus at Edfu, Egypt, was begun by Ptolemy III Euergetes I in 237 BCE and officially finished in 57 BCE, about 180 years later. Yale's Tell Edfu project calls it the best example of Ptolemaic temple building in Egypt; the complex is a little over 140 m long, with pylon towers about 36 m high.

uncertainty.note: Start is 237 BCE (Yale; ancient-egypt.co.uk gives 23 August 237 BC); the temple was officially finished in 57 BCE. End is the present.

reviewer_note: Shape block (a pylon-fronted temple; no colonnade plan was sourced). Yale gives the pylon towers as 'approximately 36m in height' and the temple as 'little over 140m long', area about 7000 m2; no width was found. A Heidelberg study seen only in search snippets gave 32.5 m and ~70 m; it was not opened. Dates: Yale says Ptolemy III began in 237 BCE and Ptolemy VIII inaugurated it in 142 BCE; the main door was fitted in 57 BCE.
